---
title: Configuration
---

`biblint` keeps policy in `biblint.toml`.
The command line chooses what to run and how to report it; it does not define the formatting policy.

## Discovery

Without `--config`, biblint searches for `biblint.toml` from the input path upward.
An explicitly supplied `--config` path takes precedence.
A repository should normally commit one configuration file at its root so editors, local runs, and CI use the same settings.

The top-level file-selection settings apply to both `check` and `format`:

```toml
include = ["**/*.bib"]
exclude = ["vendor/**"]
default-exclude = true
```

Directories recursively contribute files whose extension is `.bib`.
Explicit file arguments are accepted regardless of extension.
With the default excludes enabled, `.git/**` and `target/**` are skipped.

## Rule selection

```toml
[lint]
# `select` replaces the default rule set.
select = ["duplicate_key", "duplicate_doi"]

# `extend-select` adds rules without removing defaults.
extend-select = ["key_format"]

# `ignore` wins over selection.
ignore = ["unsupported_escape"]

[lint.per-file-ignores]
"generated/**" = ["formatting"]
```

Use `all` in a selection or ignore list as a wildcard.
If `select` is omitted, the default-enabled rules run.
`extend-select` is useful for opt-in rules such as `key_format`, `duplicate_doi`, `duplicate_citation`, and `duplicate_abstract`.
Per-file ignores use the same rule names and are applied after global selection.

## Starter configuration

This is a reasonable repository-level starting point:

```toml
include = ["**/*.bib"]
exclude = ["vendor/**", "generated/**"]
default-exclude = true

[lint]
extend-select = ["duplicate_doi", "duplicate_citation", "key_format"]

[lint.key-format]
style = "better-bibtex"

[format]
indent = 2
align = false
lowercase = true
sort = ["key"]
sort-fields = ["title", "author", "year"]

[format.key-generation]
formula = "auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1,0)"
```

The formula is optional here because it is biblint's default.
The full formula surface is documented in [Citekey generation](key-generation.md).

## Configuration rules

Unknown settings are rejected rather than ignored.
Formula syntax is validated when the configuration is loaded, including formulas in `[format.key-generation]`.
Invalid globs and unknown rule names are also configuration errors.
This keeps a misspelled policy from looking like a successful clean run.

Formatting settings are deserialized with defaults, so a small file can change one policy without repeating every other setting:

```toml
[format]
blank-lines = true
sort = ["key"]
```
